items.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21
items.q: I know what it was good, but the Padukas that was playing with them fellas out there.

ctx.x: Eh? When they slipped a Fuduki in there and beat the game. That's right. I was there that time. They slipped two fellas in there, a rabbit and a Fuduki, and they slipped them and fell in there and they had them. They had them about. Yeah. Sweevers was eating them up. Yeah. The Sweevers, and they slipped them, but I don't know how they felt slipping in there. A rabbit got behind the bat and Fuduki and everything. They said, shout Fuduki, and they were shouting too. I told them they had to get fished for me. I knew…

Paduka was a pitcher? And the rabbit was the catcher? Yeah. And how they slipped them two fellas in there, them fellas was running away with them. Yeah. But the Paduka had to slip them two fellas in there. I'd stand up there and every time they'd strike them fellas out, every time they'd go in. And he used to do that shout. All he used to say, shout Fuduki. A large mascot. A large mascot. A large mascot. A large mascot. Fuduki. And they picked him up and carried him away in the ballroom. They told him. They told…
